title: 🤖 A Swarm of 32 AI Agents Speeds Up Coding 19 Times — and the Secret Is in the Organization!
body: 🤖 A Swarm of 32 AI Agents Speeds Up Coding 19 Times — and the Secret Is in the Organization!

Replit revealed on November 19 the results of a new experiment measuring how swarms of AI agents work on software-acceleration tasks, through a new test called Optimization Bench covering 14 open-source software libraries. On tasks for the famous NumPy library, a single Claude Opus 5.5 agent made code 3.7 times faster in two hours, while a swarm of 32 agents reached a speedup of 18.9 times in the same time.

The surprise was that the strongest single agent was not the best team player: GPT-6.2 Astra was the strongest alone on every task, but its swarms got worse as they grew — falling below its solo result on three of four tasks at 32 agents. The reason is the organization method: the successful swarms communicated through a shared board everyone could read, while Astra's swarms sent everything by direct messages to the coordinator, until his inbox became a bottleneck choking the whole team.

In the best experiment, the coordinator sent no message to any worker in the 32-agent swarm — instead distributing the work, waiting, and merging the results. The experiment also showed that the shape of the work itself determines the outcome: independent tasks scale with the team, while tasks that overlap in the same files, such as Git tasks, limit the benefit of adding more agents.

Simply put: imagine a team of 32 programmers working without meetings, each announcing what they are working on on a board everyone can see — that is what worked, while the team that sent everything to the manager alone choked.
Would you prefer a team of AI agents or a single expert programmer?
